"Insulation slows heat transfer primarily by increasing resistance to conduction, convection, and radiation. Heat moves from high to low temperature. In conduction, Fourier's law: Qdot = -k A (dT/dx). k is thermal conductivity. Insulation materials have low k (e.g., foam, fiberglass, aerogel) and trapped air has very low k. Adding thickness increases path length L, lowering heat flow proportionally. In convection, insulation fills voids and irregularities, reducing gaps where air can circulate; it also creates stagnant boundary layers, lowering convective heat transfer coefficient h. In radiation, ordinary insulation may not stop all radiation; low-emissivity coatings or reflective barriers reduce radiative heat transfer. Total resistance is sum: R = L/(kA) plus convection/radiation resistances.

For a GPU, thermal insulation might be a thermal pad, case foam, or shroud. It slows heat moving from GPU die through heatsink to air, or from component to ambient. However, if too much, it can cause hot spots and reduce cooling. In active cooling, insulation slows unwanted heat spreading but must allow convection to heatsink. The principle: lower thermal conductivity, increased distance, trapped air, reduced convection, and reduced radiation all lower heat flux. Insulation does not stop heat transfer; it increases thermal resistance, so temperature gradient drives slower transfer."
